subject.title: feat: parents get durable state-change notices when humans interact with child sessions

question: After the two lifecycle-boundary defects are fixed, should OpenClaw adopt this durable event log and proactive parent invalidation as the canonical core session-reconciliation contract?
rationale: The repair is mechanical, but the PR establishes new persistent data, model-facing semantics, retention behavior, and best-effort failure guarantees that require explicit product and ownership intent.

options.title: Fix then adopt
options.body: Resolve both P1 findings, prove fresh-install and upgrade behavior, and accept the durable protocol as the canonical core path.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Ship only `stateVersion` and `changesSince` while deferring proactive notices until a simpler committed-delivery hook exists.

options.title: Pause the protocol
options.body: Keep current task and completion-announcement behavior until maintainers define a smaller persistent contract.

recommendation.title: Fix then adopt
recommendation.body: Resolve both P1 findings, prove fresh-install and upgrade behavior, and accept the durable protocol as the canonical core path.
